thread:
emma: quick sync — proposal to rebalance token-slab ceilings per card family. ran a small profile and some heuristics look promising.
raj: share numbers?
emma: profile snapshot (p50 throughput tokens/sec, kv frag %, median seq len):

```
A10  |  18k tok/s  | KV frag 12% | med len 40
T4   |   9k tok/s  | KV frag 18% | med len 36
L4   |  11k tok/s  | KV frag 22% | med len 28
A100 |  28k tok/s  | KV frag 8%  | med len 48
H100 |  31k tok/s  | KV frag 6%  | med len 50
```

emma: baseline we had a single global max_tokens_per_batch=20k which is causing either underutilization on A100/H100 or KV thrash on L4/T4.
cheng: that 22% KV frag on L4 explains the latency spikes we saw in canary last week.
liz: can we do per-card ceilings that account for kv-frag overhead and kernel fit? e.g. reduce effective slab for L4/T4 and boost for A100/H100.
raj: yes — something like: compute ceiling = floor(raw_throughput * med_seq * safety_factor) then clamp by kernel-fit thresholds.
emma: exact numbers I prototyped:

```
max_tokens_per_batch = {
  "a10": "16000",
  "t4":  "8000",
  "l4":  "9000",
  "a100": "26000",
  "h100": "28000"
}
safety_factor = 0.85  # kv/cold penalties
```

matt: those look sane. need to validate tail latencies — p99 is what ops cares about.
infra-bot: deploy-checklist created: perf-experiment/1748209987 — canary group set to 5% traffic, metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, kernel-fallback-count, kv-frag-rate.
cheng: one caution — kernel selector sometimes switches to slower kernels when batchshape changes. we should pin kernel policy for initial canary.
emma: good catch. i'll add a canary override: kernel_policy: prefer_low_frag when frag > 15%.
liz: also add a metric for 'pack_ratio' (tokens packed / tokens allowed) so we can detect underpacking on A100.
raj: agree. if pack_ratio < 0.7 for >10min, mark canary unhealthy.
emma: action items: 
- emma: push canary config + telemetry (today)
- cheng: add kernel_policy override to selector (WIP)
- liz: dashboard for pack_ratio + kv-frag per card family
- matt: run regression job for L4 at +10% load after canary

emma: any objections to those numbers before I land the experiment? :eyes:
matt: :thumbsup: go ahead, but gate by p99 and kernel-fallback < 2/min.
raj: add a quick smoke script to replay real request traces (short seq + long seq mix) against the canary config.
emma: will do. will post results in this thread.
